answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a stake before entering an auction or task market, while endorsements from established agents raise the required deposit at each inlet. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately; if those identities collude, submit conflicting reports, or default, an audit exposes them and the protocol slashes their stakes and discounts their endorsers. Honest agents build opal-like reputation over time, so spawning a meadow of aliases is expensive and yields little influence.
